Figure 1:Few-step generative perplexity on LM1B(lower is better,HH= sample entropy).
E-MoE gives markedly lower generative perplexity than both factorized MDLM(Sahoo et al., 2024)and continuous-latent VADD(Xie et al., 2026)for all NFEs 1–16, at matched sample entropy.

Figure 4:Generation results on 2-D toy examples.Ground truth and generations of MDLM(Sahoo et al., 2024), VADD(Xie et al., 2026), and E-MoE at NFE=1=1on 8-modes and swiss-roll. Full sweeps over NFE∈{1,2,8,32}\in\{1,2,8,32\}are in AppendixC.1.
Figure 6:Full NFE sweep generations on 8-modes, NFE∈{1,2,8,32}\in\{1,2,8,32\}. MDLM smears mass into a blurred grid even at NFE=32=32. VADD and E-MoE both recover the eight clusters from NFE=1=1.

Figure 7:Full NFE sweep generations on Swiss-roll, NFE∈{1,2,8,32}\in\{1,2,8,32\}. MDLM spreads its mass over the whole disk at low NFE and concentrates on the spiral only by NFE=32=32. VADD and E-MoE both recover the spiral from NFE=1=1.

Figure 8:Binarized-MNIST samples across NFE, the first1616draws from a fixed seed per cell. MDLM gives unstructured speckle at NFE≤2\leq 2and resolves digits only by NFE=10=10–2020, while E-MoE produces recognizable digits from a single step.
